A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same guidance framework and research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-classification, copy-paste, parity and language-modeling experiments, plus appendix experiments using noise, MSE loss and RSA alignment.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds larger language models, distillation comparisons, geometric analyses, intrinsic-dimensionality regularization and layer-selection ablations.

M1.justification: The core frozen-guide objective remains, but v2 adds an intrinsic-dimensionality regularization loss (Appendix I.2) and projected ridge-regression alignment (J.2). It also replaces guidance disconnected during task training with alignment-only initialization on noise before unguided task training. Algorithm 1 changes the layer-index clipping bound from the guide-layer count to the target-layer count. These are substantive procedural additions and revisions.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet-1K and CIFAR-10 classification, WikiText-103 language modeling, copy-paste and parity. CIFAR-10 moves from the MSE experiment to layer ablations; it is not newly introduced. Larger models, probing and alternative training procedures operate within retained data and task coverage.

E2.justification: v1 discusses distillation without experimentally comparing it against guidance. v2 evaluates basic logit/KL knowledge distillation with trained and untrained teachers across image and sequence settings (Figure 5), and adds Deep FCN loss and error-consistency comparisons in Appendix H. This supplies a substantive new comparator for the paper's central distinction.

E3.justification: The documented language-model target changes from a five-layer, 512-unit tanh RNN to a four-layer ReLU model, with an additional six-layer, 1024-unit model using context length 128. Table 4 changes guided copy-paste learning rates from 1e-5 to 1e-4 and guided language-model rates from 5e-5 to 1e-4. Initialization changes from disconnecting guidance after 150 task-training steps to 300 alignment-only steps. These are reported setting changes, not evidence that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds tests of layer selection and mapping, early versus late alignment dynamics, guide-to-guide similarity, intrinsic-dimensionality trajectories and intervention, linear decodability, and ridge alignment. These investigate design choices and possible mechanisms absent from v1. The initialization analysis is revised, while v1's CIFAR-10 MSE-loss ablation is removed. Noise-fed guidance and RSA analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five random seeds, standard-error reporting and selection using the lowest seed-averaged validation loss. The v2 checklist reiterates this practice without adding a statistical procedure or increasing the stated run count. Changed standard-error values belong to E6.

E6.justification: v2 adds large-RNN perplexities of 89.13 unguided, 36.91 with a trained guide and 47.17 with an untrained guide, plus distillation, layer-ablation, ridge and intrinsic-dimensionality results. Most earlier headline means remain, but untrained-Transformer perplexity changes from 51948.8 to 5.19e5, and Deep/Wide FCN standard errors change from 0.51/1.21 to 1.21/0.91. Initialization findings are replaced and MSE results removed. Results under added or revised settings do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix I.2 introduces a substantive mathematical construction of an intrinsic-dimensionality penalty using singular values, cumulative explained variance and sigmoid penalties, particularly Equations 10–14. Appendix J.2 also formalizes projected ridge alignment. Existing CKA, RSA and error-consistency mathematics largely remains. The discussion of prior generalization theory does not provide a new guidance-specific theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central claims about transferring architectural priors and rescuing unsuitable networks remain. v2 strengthens the initialization claim from evidence that better initializations likely exist to an explicit guidance-only initialization scheme, and its conclusion adds evidence of scaling within models of 150M parameters or fewer. These refine rather than replace the main contribution.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands mechanism explanations: locality and weight sharing reflected in alignment statistics, connections to kernel/generalization theory, delayed intrinsic-dimensionality collapse, and layer-dependent credit assignment. It uses linear decoding to argue against readily accessible class information explaining random-guide benefits. Appendix I.1 explicitly leaves a guidance-specific proof unresolved. These extend well beyond the retained explanations about architectural priors and trained features.

D1.justification: v2 provides additional reproducibility details, including distillation temperature 2 and weight 0.5, ridge penalties 10 and 100, projection and representation-splitting procedures, and linear-probe sample counts of 4000 training and 1000 validation images. Architecture descriptions and learning-rate tables are updated. The abstract replaces the direct code-repository link with a project website; actual online availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning through FitNets, teacher-guided architecture search, random-feature learning, intrinsic dimensionality and theoretical representation alignment. Appendix I.1 newly connects guidance to work by Insulla and colleagues, Baratin and colleagues, and Shan and Bordelon. Several earlier distillation and canonical-correlation references are removed. This changes the scientific framing beyond citation-format updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, results and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting and compression. Sequence modeling precedes vision, numbered experimental subsections become shorter thematic paragraphs, and CKA details, alignment-loss analysis and error-consistency mathematics move into reorganized appendices. A NeurIPS checklist is added. These are extensive narrative and structural changes.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, and Figure 2 combines previously separate training/validation panels while adding the larger language model. The main result tables are reordered and expanded. The original alignment-loss figure is split into appendix displays; initialization plots are replaced, the MSE plot disappears, and new distillation, geometry, probing and ablation displays are added. The document also adopts conference formatting.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important evidential gaps: the distinction from logit distillation is directly tested, and previously untested layer-mapping choices receive informative ablations (Figure 5; Appendices H and K). Initialization-only training and the geometric intervention further strengthen the paper's explanatory value. These gains outweigh removal of the MSE generality test. Reporting weaknesses remain: the language-model prose overstates some Table 2 gains, and setting inconsistencies limit interpretation of scaling. The improvement rests on stronger controls and targeted analyses, not higher headline scores.
